canonical_data: Typed per-dataset indices built by `xerj autoindex` from whatever a folder contains (code with tree-sitter symbols, docs, logs, PDFs, SQLite, CSV), plus a separate namespaced `/_memory` store, all held on local disk under the configured data directory.
strengths: Elasticsearch API compatibility means existing clients, dashboards, and agent tooling work against it unchanged, rather than adopting a new query language
Tree-sitter-aware code ingestion returns symbols and file:line locations rather than flat text, which is the specific retrieval shape a coding agent's reference-coding workflow needs
A single static binary with an offline default embedder needs no server, database, or model download to start, and stays usable on a host with no runtime internet access
weaknesses: Pre-1.0: the project is eleven weeks old and, as of this review, has shipped seventy-four release candidates and no stable 1.0.0, so its interface and index format should be treated as still moving

The README's stated membership ask, that any user or agent who runs it send back a one-file field-report pull request, is documented to work identically whether a human or an agent installed it mid-session in someone else's codebase; that mechanic can inflate contributor, pull-request, and fork counts as an adoption signal, and neither should be read as independent evidence of organic usage

The default local run mode is `--insecure`, with no TLS and no authentication; the alternative mode auto-generates an API key file on first boot rather than offering an account or tenant model, so there is no built-in multi-user access control beyond that one key

The measured token-reduction claims (2.7x fewer output tokens than a grepping agent) are the vendor's own case study on its own benchmark; they are evidence of what the study measured, not an independently reproduced result
why_it_matters: A concrete, working answer to the token cost of an agent reading source files one at a time: index a corpus once with no schema, then retrieve typed, symbol-aware passages through a protocol every existing search client already speaks.
